organisms.name: Escherichia coli K-12
organisms.strain_scope: K-12 protein sources; not every K-12 derivative or condition
organisms.envelope_summary: Diderm envelope: inner membrane, periplasm with peptidoglycan, outer membrane. Outer-membrane protein loops face an LPS-containing environment.

sources.claim: Cryo-TEM observations of K-12 envelope layers and preparation-dependent variation.

organisms.limits: Rod represented by a smooth ellipsoid. Dimensions, layer gaps and thickness are illustrative display choices, not segmented or quantitatively reconstructed from this paper. LPS/cell-wall polymers are not built.
organisms.overview_evidence_state: literature-informed schematic; no segmented organism mesh

molecular_preparation.reason: Organism metadata alone does not supply compatible chemistry, topology or hydration settings.

organisms.name: Bacillus subtilis
organisms.strain_scope: KtrAB/TasA: strain 168; OpuAC structure: species-level record, exact matched strain not established
organisms.envelope_summary: Cytoplasmic membrane with an external peptidoglycan/teichoic-acid wall region. Membrane proteins can lie beneath the outer wall; extracellular does not guarantee unobstructed access.

sources.claim: Frozen-hydrated sections of strain 168 distinguish low-density inner and polymeric outer wall zones.
OpuAC is an extracellular ligand-binding component of OpuA, with membrane-tethered lipoprotein context.

organisms.limits: Paper measurements are condition/preparation-specific means, not universal parameters. Display dimensions/gaps are illustrative. OPM hydrophobic boundaries are distinct from microscopy total membrane thickness. TasA monomer is not a native fibril.
organisms.overview_evidence_state: literature-informed schematic; no segmented organism mesh

molecular_preparation.reason: Organism metadata alone does not supply compatible chemistry, topology or hydration settings.

organisms.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
organisms.strain_scope: Pma1: S288C; Ste2: species-level/mixed yeast entity annotations; no identical strain/condition claim
organisms.envelope_summary: Plasma membrane beneath a cell wall. Ste2 receptors and Pma1 pumps belong to the plasma membrane; their presence does not establish exposure beyond the wall.

sources.claim: Cryo-ET-informed yeast geometry explicitly distinguishes plasma membrane, cell wall and extracellular regions.
Primary whole-cell geometry study; current viewer does not use its tomographic segmentation.

organisms.limits: Sphere, radius and wall gap are illustrative. Budding/scars, wall architecture and native protein abundance/locations are not reconstructed. Experimental membrane complexes contain intracellular domains and engineered states.
organisms.overview_evidence_state: literature-informed schematic; no segmented organism mesh
